metadata.hardware_requirements: computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: A series of simulation experiments based on real-world traffic data are conducted to evaluate the proposed approach.
nodes_source.description: Traffic volume data from a freeway connecting Qingdao and Huangdao in Shandong, China. Used to calibrate microscopic traffic simulation parameters in SUMO and evaluate the proposed DRL model.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Available from the corresponding author upon request, as explicitly stated in the Data Availability section.

nodes_process.source_quote: Vehicle locations from raw images are extracted to reconstruct visual representations
nodes_process.description: Extracts vehicle position (xi, yi) from raw video frames to create a binary position matrix mt for each time step. Positions include the signal light status (UG/UR). Down-sampling is applied.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, generic tool specified but mapping details for (xi, yi) are summary; parameter stated for final dimensions.

nodes_process.source_quote: we stack the matrices of consecutive N time steps to represent the state st
nodes_process.description: Concatenates position matrices from N consecutive time steps into a single state tensor st = {mt-(N-1), ..., mt} for input into the DRL agent.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, parameters and logic fully specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: A multitask learning strategy is implemented in the training process to improve learning efficiency.
nodes_process.description: Trains a CNN-based Q-network with a dual-output head (action value and auxiliary task: speed/queue prediction). Uses Experience Replay and Target Networks for stability.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, all architecture and training hyperparams in Table 1 and Fig 7.

nodes_process.source_quote: The proposed method is evaluated in SUMO, an open-source microscopic traffic simulator
nodes_process.description: Compares DRL control with No-Control and PI-ALINEA baselines over 20 simulation experiments in a real-world tunnel merging scenario. Calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, environment and baseline params fully specified.

nodes_process.source_quote: The control area is divided into eight subareas... information in the subarea is removed from original data
nodes_process.description: Evaluates sensitivity to data availability by masking individual spatial subareas of the input video data and observing performance impact on mean travel time.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, methodology well described; requires manual subarea division shown in Fig 15.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Mean vehicle travel times (s) for no controls, PI-ALINEA, and DRL across 20 experiments including performance comparison percentages.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Uses SUMO and provided parameters; source traffic data available upon request. Coherent mapping from simulation runs to mean results.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 8: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time.
nodes_sink.description: Graphs showing reward and mainline travel time over 1,000,000 training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: RL training outcomes are specified; parameters provided, though data requested and random seeds omitted.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Quartile time series of mainline travel times between 8:00 and 9:00 for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear statistical derivation from stated scenarios and open simulator.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10: Temporal-spatial distribution of speed in (a) no-control; (b) PI-ALINEA; (c) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Heatmaps showing speed variation over space (mainline distance) and time (8:00-9:00).
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Inputs from specified simulator; visualization method (temporal-spatial distribution) is standard.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: On-ramp queue lengths over time showing distribution ranges for control scenarios.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Consistent derivation from SUMO simulator output metrics.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12: Relationship of queue length and red ratio for (a) PI-ALINEA and (b) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plots and regression showing queue length vs signal red ratio.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Claim regarding red-ratio utilization is clearly plotted from available scenario outcomes.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13: Queue length and occupancy for (a) PI-ALINEA and (b) DRL.
nodes_sink.description: Dual-axis time series plotting downstream occupancy and queue length.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Directly derivable from simulation time-step logs.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 14: Downstream volume in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Box plots of vehicle throughput over 5-minute intervals between 8:00 and 9:00.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Throughput data readily produced by stated simulation settings.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed
nodes_sink.description: Box plot comparison of baseline travel times against scenarios with perturbed visual inputs from subareas 1-8.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Sensitivity test follows clear protocol based on Figure 15 mapping, though data availability is restrictive.
